transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-14
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Sofia (CTO, Horizon), Liam (Head Infra), Rajesh (ML Platform), Emily (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick renewal check plus discussion about expansion: Horizon wants to add dedicated capacity for peak volumes, expand to EU and APAC regions, and lock in pricing for contract extension. Customer asked about benchmarks, security / SOC2 and networking (VPC), and timeline for procurement. Next steps: send updated quote, schedule benchmark, share security docs, procurement to send redline.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, appreciate you making time. This is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, and with me I have Ethan (SE) and Priya our CSM.
[00:10] Sofia: Hey Maya, thanks, hi team. We've got Liam, Rajesh and Emily on our side. Appreciate the time.
[00:16] Maya: Great, quick agenda — renewal status, capacity needs for Q1, adding EU/APAC, and any security/procurement blockers. Sound good?
[00:24] Liam: Yep sounds good. We'll probably dive straight into numbers — our peak qps has been climbing.
[00:30] Ethan: Cool, maybe I can start with the performance summary — the dedicated pools we've provisioned have given you the consistent p99s, but I think for the spikes you mentioned, moving to 3x dedicated nodes with a burst policy will smooth out the tail latency.
[00:42] Rajesh: Yeah, the p99 is fine right now at ~220ms but our burst windows during EOD are killing us, we saw up to 800ms last month. Curious about autoscale and burst credits.
[00:55] Ethan: Right, so our dedicated offering supports a configurable burst capacity and queue prioritization. There's also prefix/KV cache to shave off repeated context — that helps a lot for your template-based responses.
[01:08] Sofia: Is the KV cache multi-region? If we add EU and APAC, will cache misses become a problem?
[01:14] Ethan: Good question. Currently cache is per-region to keep latencies low and data locality clean; we can set up cross-region replication for hotspots but there's tradeoff on eventual consistency. For most setups we recommend region-local cache + smart routing.
[01:28] Liam: So we'd want EU region for regulatory reasons (clients in EMEA), and APAC for latency to our Sydney nodes. What's the lead time to turn on a new region?
[01:37] Maya: Typically 2-3 weeks to provision dedicated pools in a new cloud region once contract and capacity are confirmed, sometimes faster if we use hosted capacity as a stopgap.
[01:47] Emily: Okay procurement note — we need to know pricing up front, and ideally a 12-month committed rate versus on-demand. Can you provide both?
[01:54] Maya: Yes we'll put both in the quote. For committed we can give a discount based on committed vGPU hours. I'll include options: monthly reserved for Dedicated and an overage burst buffer.
[02:05] Rajesh: Also, quantization profiles — we want to push smaller models for cost but keep quality. Does Redwood have model/quant recommendations per workload?
[02:12] Ethan: Yes, Redwood Optimize will recommend quant settings based on your evals. We can run a quick eval on your prompt set during the benchmark and show the expected cost/latency delta.
[02:23] Sofia: That would be great. On security — SOC2, SSO, KMS — we've had questions from InfoSec.
[02:29] Priya: I'll send our SOC2 report and SSO + KMS integration docs after the call. For Private deployment we also support customer-managed KMS and HSMs for key custody.
[02:40] Emily: Any gotchas for our security team regarding logs or data residency?
[02:44] Priya: Audit logs are available; retention windows configurable. For data residency, Private or region-specific Dedicated keeps the data within the selected region — that'll meet EMEA requirements.
[02:56] Liam: Network-wise we need a VPC peering option, and ideally a diagram of the network flow for our firewall team.
[03:03] Maya: We'll attach a network diagram, and our SE will include the recommended firewall rules and IPs.
[03:10] Rajesh: Back to performance, can we run a benchmark with our actual traffic profile? We want to see p50/p95/p99 across different sequence lengths.
[03:17] Ethan: Absolutely. We'll need a sample workload and expected concurrency profile. We can run the benchmark on a dedicated pool and on a hosted-compatible setup so you can compare. Typical plan is 2 hours including baseline + KV cache + batching scenarios.
[03:30] Sofia: Timeline-wise, procurement wants to finalize by end of month, so we need quotes and security docs early next week ideally.
[03:36] Maya: Understood. We'll aim to get everything over by Tuesday.
[03:40] Emily: One more procurement question — are there auto-renewal clauses we should be aware of? We usually push back on automatic renewals.
[03:47] Maya: Our standard contract includes renewal options but not automatic renewal without explicit notice; we can surface that in the term sheet and accept redlines.
[03:55] Rajesh: Regarding competitors — we've evaluated Anthorpic and SageMaker endpoints; Anthropic had better contextual understanding on some tests but the economics were rough. Any notes?
[04:05] Ethan: Yeah we've seen that — Anthorpic tends to be strong for safety-sensitive prompts but at higher cost; SageMaker gives you control but you pay infra ops. Redwood tries to optimize for unit economics with caching & batching so you get lower per-token costs.
[04:20] Sofia: Good. For the quote, include a scenario with 3x dedicated pools + 1x burst buffer, and an option with hosted fallback for peak events.
[04:30] Maya: Will do. We'll also include regional add-ons for EU and APAC.
[04:36] Liam: For SLA — is there an SLA delta for dedicated vs hosted? We need p99 SLA guarantees for our consumer-facing API.
[04:44] Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include the SLA language. Hosted has a best-effort SLA at a lower price point.
[04:53] Emily: Any penalties or credits?
[04:55] Priya: Yes, the Dedicated SLA includes credits for downtime; we'll include the exact thresholds in the doc.
[05:02] Rajesh: For the benchmark, can you simulate KV cache warm starts vs cold? We saw a 40% gap when cache was cold previously.
[05:10] Ethan: Yep we'll script both scenarios, and include continuous batching to match your concurrency. Also to note — sequence length distribution will affect throughput heavily, so share that and we'll tune kernel/quant profiles.
[05:23] Sofia: On the legal side, we may need a mutual NDA extension for the benchmarking data.
[05:27] Emily: Yeah procurement will require it.
[05:29] Maya: We can add a short addendum; I'll coordinate with legal.
[05:33] Liam: Anything else on pricing? Also curious about minimum commitments — is there a minimum vGPU commitment?
[05:39] Maya: Minimums are flexible; for Dedicated we typically see a 6-12 month commit. We'll show pricing tiers starting at 1 node equivalent.
[05:47] Sofia: Great. If we proceed, what does onboarding look like? How long to production?
[05:53] Priya: Onboarding usually takes 2-4 weeks: setup, VPC peering, SSO, then a pilot run and performance tuning. We'll run an onboarding checklist with milestones.
[06:03] Rajesh: Ok let's aim for a pilot in November if procurement moves quickly.
[06:07] Maya: Sounds good — to recap: Redwood sends updated quote with committed vs on-demand pricing, includes EU & APAC region costs, SLA language, and security docs. SE schedules benchmark with Rajesh, and procurement to share redlines.
[06:20] Emily: I'll get the redline by Oct 22.
[06:23] Maya: Great, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark once Ethan proposes times. Thanks everyone.
[06:29] Sofia: Thanks all.
[06:31] End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcription, speaker overlaps minimal; some product names were slightly mis-transcribed ("Anthorpic" instead of Anthropic). References: shared sheet (link: drive.google.com/.../horizon-benchmark), network diagram (attached after call).
